Maintenance Report — MNT-0143-009

Asset: WELL-0143 (NE-07 Well 143, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 14 Jun 2024 08:00 · Finished: 15 Jun 2024 02:00 · Well stopped for this job: 18 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0143-0054 on 2024-06-13 Report written: 16 Jun 2024

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0143-0054 at 12:15 on 2024-06-13 found crude oil on the pad: about 8.2% of the pad area, estimated 4.8 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 5.2 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

Root cause

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Cleaned free oil out of the cellar.
  2. Unbolted the flange and removed the failed gasket.
  3. Fitted a new gasket and new bolts, torqued to specification.
  4. Excavated the stained soil around the cellar.

Summary of the fix: replaced the flange gasket and bolts and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 210 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 168 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 2.9 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0143-009 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.77% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0143-010

Asset: WELL-0143 (NE-07 Well 143, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 06 Sep 2024 08:00 · Finished: 10 Sep 2024 14:00 · Well stopped for this job: 102 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0143-0066 on 2024-09-05 Report written: 12 Sep 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the wellhead was cold and the pump jack was straining with a heavy, uneven load. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0143-0066 showed the wellhead at 38.3 °C with the air at 32.4 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 2 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

A worn plunger that let sand settle and lock the pump.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.

maintenance.action: Replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0143-020

Asset: WELL-0143 (NE-07 Well 143, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 03 Jan 2026 08:00 · Finished: 13 Jan 2026 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 250 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward, Kevin Price · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0143-0134 on 2026-01-01 Report written: 15 Jan 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0143-0134 showed the wellhead at 5.6 °C with the air at 5.8 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 8 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Winding breakdown from heat and age.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

  • Summer heat raises the risk of motor trips on this field.
